name: Spondyloepimetaphyseal Dysplasia with Joint Laxity, Beighton Type
aliases: SEMD with Joint Laxity, Beighton Type

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Radiological Diagnostic Criteria for SEMD with Joint Laxity, Beighton Type

criteria.description: Generalized joint hypermobility assessed by Beighton score
Radiographic evidence of spondyloepimetaphyseal dysplasia including vertebral flattening and metaphyseal irregularities
Clinical presentation of disproportionate short stature with short trunk
Presence of myopia or retinal detachment as supportive features
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of generalized joint laxity with radiographic evidence of SEMD and disproportionate short-trunk dwarfism
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not always conclusive due to genetic heterogeneity.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Generalized joint hypermobility with high Beighton score

common.symptomName: Metaphyseal irregularities and epiphyseal abnormalities on imaging
Delayed motor milestones due to musculoskeletal abnormalities

occasional.symptomName: Mild respiratory restriction due to thoracic cage abnormalities
searchTerms: reduced lung capacity due to chest shape

imaging: Platyspondyly with vertebral flattening on spine X-rays
Metaphyseal irregularities and epiphyseal dysplasia on long bone radiographs
Possible scoliosis and thoracic cage deformities
genetic: Genetic heterogeneity with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
other: High Beighton score indicating generalized joint hypermobility

distinguishingFeatures: More severe short stature with earlier onset
Different radiographic pattern with more pronounced epiphyseal involvement
Prominent ocular abnormalities including vitreoretinal degeneration
Facial dysmorphism such as midface hypoplasia

redFlags: Progressive neurological symptoms suggesting spinal cord compression
Severe respiratory compromise due to thoracic deformities
Sudden visual loss indicating retinal detachment
